result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens returning `response` from a raw `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` when sharing is enabled, while the zoho-bigin CalendarService wraps an axios call and then checks `tokenInfo.data.error` (line: `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)`). A fetch Response has no `data` property, so in sharing mode `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and reading `.error` throws, breaking every zoho-bigin token refresh once credential-sync env vars are set.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, executes `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `tokenInfo` is assigned from `await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, but immediately treated like an Axios response: `if (!tokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`. A Fetch `Response` has no `.data`, so in sharing mode this would throw (or at least `tokenInfo.data` is undefined), breaking Zoho Bigin token refresh whenever the sharing-mode env vars are configured.
